citation: Krien, U., Schönfeldt, P., Launer, J., Hilpert, S., Kaldemeyer, C., Pleßmann, G. (2020). oemof.solph - A model generator for linear and mixed-integer linear optimisation of energy systems. Software Impacts 6, 100028. doi:10.1016/j.simpa.2020.100028
description: oemof.solph is a model generator for energy system modelling and optimisation, the core package of the Open Energy Modelling Framework (oemof). Users describe an energy system as a graph of buses, converters, sources, sinks and storage components, and the package builds and solves a linear or mixed-integer linear programme for least-cost dispatch and, optionally, investment in components, covering electricity, heat, gas and other carriers in one model. It is developed and maintained by the oemof e.V. association and a community of contributors from universities and research institutes. The tool is generic and location independent: coverage and time resolution are set by the user's data, from a single building or district heating network to a national system. It is available as a Python package on PyPI (version 0.6.5, September 2026, Python 3.10 or newer), with source code on GitHub and documentation on read-the-docs, under the MIT licence at no cost. Caveats: an optimisation solver must be installed separately (open-source and commercial solvers both work), and the package formulates flows between components as a linear or mixed-integer programme, so it does not compute electrical power flow physics. Simulation uses are capacity planning and optimisation of multi-carrier systems, including district heating. Related records: it is an alternative to model-pypsa and model-calliope for energy system optimisation.
